summary: Charles James Rodgers was an Indologist and historian who studied at Borough Road College and the University of Cambridge. He served as Principal of the Christian Vernacular Education Society Training College, Amritsar (1863) and Honorary Numismatist to the Government of India (~1888-1892).

Charles Johnston was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Trinity College Dublin from circa 1886 to 1888. In 1908, he served as Special Lecturer in Political Science at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Charles Jones Ogden was an Indologist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Columbia University (~1896-1900) under A. V. Williams Jackson (~1900-1909), and later served as Columbia's Honorary Lecturer in Indo-Iranian Languages (1926-1931).

Charles Lecoutere was a linguist who studied under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin at KU Leuven, earning his Ph.D. between circa 1887 and 1892. He later served as a professor at KU Leuven from 1895.

Charles Li is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and computational studies who earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge (2014-2018). He held posts at the CNRS (2020-2023) and became Arbeitsstellenleiter at the University of Hamburg in 2023.

Charles Louis Fabri was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist who studied at the University of Pécs, Leiden University under Jean Philippe Vogel, and under Sylvain Lévi. His career included roles at Leiden University, the Lahore Museum, and National Museum, New Delhi.

Charles Malamoud is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who was educated at the University of Paris. He held academic posts at the University of Lyon (~1965-1972) and served as Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1979-1998).

Charles Masson was an archaeologist, historian, and Indologist. During his career, he served as an agent for the East India Company from circa 1822 to 1826 and for the Government of India from circa 1835 to 1838.

Charles Matthew Whish was an Indologist and historian who studied at the East India Company College (~1809-1811) and the College of Fort St. George (1812). He served with the East India Company (1812-1833), including posts in the Madras Presidency.

Charles Michel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at KU Leuven under Félix Nève and at the University of Paris under Abel Bergaigne. He served as a professor at Ghent University (1885-1892) and the University of Liège (1892-1923).

Charles Norman Seddon worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Balliol College, Oxford (1889-1891), he served as Reader in Persian and Marathi at the University of Oxford in 1924.
Charles Oman was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at New College, Oxford from circa 1878 to 1882 and held a post at the University of Oxford from circa 1883 to 1946.

Charles Otto Blagden was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. Educated at Dulwich College and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1882-1886), he later held a post at SOAS University of London from circa 1917 to 1935.

Charles Philip Brown was an Indologist and linguist who studied at East India Company College and Haileybury. Following a career in the Indian Civil Service (~1817-1855), he served as Professor of Telugu at University College London (~1855-1884).
Charles Picard was a historian and archaeologist. Over his academic career, he held positions at the University of Lyon from circa 1919 to 1934 and at the University of Paris from circa 1934 to 1955.

Charles Ramble is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Durham University and Oxford under Michael Aris. He served as a professor at Oxford (2002-2005) and became Directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2009.

Charles Rieu was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Geneva and Bonn under Christian Lassen, later serving as Curator at the British Museum and professor at UCL and Cambridge.

Charles Robert Wilson was an Indologist and historian. He was educated at the City of London School and the University of Oxford (Wadham College), later serving in the Bengal Education Department (1887) and as Principal of Patna College (~1900-1904).

Charles Rockwell Lanman was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Yale under William Dwight Whitney and James Hadley, and in Germany. He taught Sanskrit at Johns Hopkins University (1876-1880) and served as Professor at Harvard University (1880-1926).

Charles S. Prebish is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. He served for decades at Pennsylvania State University (~1972-2007) and held the Numata Chair at the University of Calgary.
